title: Computational systematics of nutritional support of vaccination against viral and bacterial pathogens as prolegomena to vaccinations against COVID-19
authors: Torshin IY; Gromova OA; Chuchalin AG
one_liner_zh: 该文研究微量营养素补充对疫苗免疫效果的影响，采用文本拓扑分析，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作、转录因子结合或AI/物理模拟建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: A total of 6,628 PUBMED-registered publications on the relationships between the effects of vaccination and the provision of micronutrients have been studied by methods of topological analysis of text data. In case of insufficient intake of certain micronutrients, the functioning of the acquired immunity is disrupted resulting in an imbalance of populations of T-cells CD4+/CD8+ and of B-lymphocytes. Nutritional supplements of folate, vitamins A, D and B12, which are recognized regulators of cell division, support a wide range of lymphocyte populations. Trace elements zinc, iron, selenium, manganese and omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids are also important for supporting the mechanisms of acquired immunity. The data presented show that a course intake of these micronutrients by patients planning vaccination can significantly improve its effectiveness. In particular, these micronutrients can increase the titers of antibodies to pathogens, and to reduce the percentage of patients who still contract infection after vaccination. Supplements of these micronutrients can also contribute to the safety of vaccination: to prevent malaise and, in the unfortunate case of contracting infection despite the vaccine, to reduce the severity of the course and the mortality from the corresponding infection.
abstract_zh: 共6,628篇PUBMED注册的关于疫苗接种效果与微量营养素供给关系的出版物，已通过文本数据拓扑分析方法进行研究。在特定微量营养素摄入不足的情况下，获得性免疫的功能会受到干扰，导致T细胞CD4+/CD8+及B淋巴细胞群体失衡。叶酸、维生素A、D和B12的营养补充剂，作为公认的细胞分裂调节因子，支持广泛的淋巴细胞群体。微量元素锌、铁、硒、锰以及omega-3多不饱和脂肪酸，对于维持获得性免疫机制同样重要。所呈现的数据表明，计划接种疫苗的患者疗程性摄入这些微量营养素，可显著提高疫苗的有效性。特别是，这些微量营养素能增加针对病原体的抗体滴度，并减少接种后仍感染感染的患者比例。这些微量营养素的补充剂还有助于疫苗接种的安全性：预防不适，并在不幸发生接种后仍感染的情况下，减轻病程严重程度及相应感染的死亡率。
